headline: High: shared filesystem and broad MCP/network surfaces make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read and write the filesystem and execute shell commands, while Semantic Kernel can read/write application-defined files and use MCP servers. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if one agent consumes the other's files or MCP outputs as trusted input. The interaction is documented only at the profile level, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF AutoGPT ingests files produced by Semantic Kernel as instructions or prompts
IF Semantic Kernel forwards MCP or file content into AutoGPT without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories
Add a manual review step before either agent consumes the other's files
Disable MCP routes that can carry untrusted content into prompts
Prefix all inter-agent files with a non-executable schema header
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and content filtering between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT has filesystem access and allowlisted egress, and Semantic Kernel reads/writes files, uses broad network egress, and handles model-provider and plugin credentials. If they share a workspace, sensitive application context or secrets can move from B into A's outputs or from A into external APIs. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this is medium, not high.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same filesystem tree
IF Semantic Kernel loads secrets or application context into files that AutoGPT can read
IF AutoGPT forwards read file contents through its allowlisted egress
mitigations: Place secrets in a separate directory inaccessible to AutoGPT
Rotate any plugin or model API keys before co-running
Restrict AutoGPT egress to a test-only endpoint
Review shared files for sensitive data before execution
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell commands and spawn subprocesses, while Semantic Kernel can write files and coordinate multiple instances via shared memory store. Even without explicit git access, overlapping writes to shared resources can race and corrupt state. Because the profiles do not show a locking mechanism or a shared directory, the conflict is plausible but not proven high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or memory store
IF AutoGPT shell actions modify files that Semantic Kernel also writes
IF no external lock or lease is enforced
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory
Serialize writes with a simple file lock or mutex
Disable concurrent runs during shared-resource updates
Snapshot the workspace before each run
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Semantic Kernel is an orchestration layer that can call plugins and OpenAPI tools, so it may treat AutoGPT-produced text as actionable context. AutoGPT can generate autonomous outputs from shell and filesystem activity, which increases the chance that B will propagate A's mistakes into downstream actions. The profiles do not show explicit verification, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF Semantic Kernel uses AutoGPT output as authoritative input to plugins or OpenAPI tools
IF no validation step checks AutoGPT's claims before action execution
mitigations: Require human approval before any external action
Add a validation prompt that checks AutoGPT outputs against source data
Limit Semantic Kernel plugins to read-only tools during testing
Log every A-to-B handoff for review
requires-engineering: implement schema validation for inter-agent messages

E_compliance.rationale: Semantic Kernel explicitly handles model-provider API keys and plugin credentials and can send data to Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, Hugging Face, MCP servers, and OpenAPI tools. AutoGPT also has network egress and filesystem access, so if regulated data enters the pair, it can be transmitted outside a controlled boundary. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so this is a compliance risk but not a proven breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into either agent's context
IF Semantic Kernel routes that data to a third-party model or MCP/OpenAPI endpoint
IF no DPA, residency control, or retention policy is configured
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents' prompts
Use tenant-approved endpoints only
Disable nonessential plugins and MCP servers
Review retention settings for each provider
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data residency and retention
